applying.label: Applying the settings
applying.done: Applied: every process runs with these settings.
applying.apiRestarting: rvav's API is starting again with these settings…
applying.running: Applying: each process finishes the work it runs, then starts again with these settings.

certificate.addedLeaf: Certificate added to the CA bundle
certificate.addedBody: Test again to check. Each process applies the bundle once its running work is done.
certificate.notAdded: Not added to the CA bundle
certificate.uncheckedTrusted: Not checked: TLS verification is off for this connection. rvav would trust it.
certificate.uncheckedUntrusted: Not checked: TLS verification is off for this connection. rvav wouldn't trust it: {{problem}}.
certificate.trusted: A CA rvav trusts vouches for it.
certificate.pinned: Pinned: trusted for this connection by its SHA-256.
certificate.label: Server certificate
certificate.inForm: Its SHA-256 is in the form: save the settings to trust it.
certificate.addLeaf: Add it to the CA bundle
certificate.bundleSetBy: The CA bundle is set by RVAV_CA_BUNDLE.
certificate.everyLeaf: Every connection will trust this certificate, not only this one's.
certificate.everyAnchor: Every connection will trust the certificates {{anchor}} signs, not only this one's.

inventoryToken.title: Inventory token
inventoryToken.madeToast: The inventory token is in AWX
inventoryToken.about: AWX's inventory source reads rvav's VMs with an API token that reads the inventory only, kept in its rvav API credential. rvav makes it for a user of its own, valid a year, and puts it in AWX; the one made before is revoked.
inventoryToken.lockedBy: Set by RVAV_INVENTORY_TOKEN: rvav awx-bootstrap puts that one in AWX.
inventoryToken.none: rvav hasn't made one: AWX reads the inventory with a token made by hand, or not at all.
inventoryToken.url: rvav's address, as AWX reaches it
inventoryToken.urlHint: Empty keeps the one in AWX's credential, or else {{url}}
inventoryToken.makeNew: Make a new token and put it in AWX
inventoryToken.make: Make a token and put it in AWX
inventoryToken.sourceFirst: Set the inventory source ID above, and save, first.
inventoryToken.inCredential: In AWX's credential <name>{{credential}}</name>, reading rvav at <url>{{url}}</url>.
inventoryToken.inCredentialAttached: In AWX's credential <name>{{credential}}</name>, now set on the inventory source, reading rvav at <url>{{url}}</url>.
inventoryToken.revoked: The token made before is revoked.

vcenters.sheetDescription: rvav syncs its inventory and builds VMs in it with this account.
vcenters.name: Name
vcenters.nameHint: How rvav calls it: placement rules and VMs name it
vcenters.testThenSave: Test again, then save the vCenter.
vcenters.title: vCenters
vcenters.description: rvav syncs and builds in every vCenter here. A placement rule may name the one its clusters are in; a cluster name in two vCenters needs it.
vcenters.emptyBody: Set the vCenter connection above, then add others here.
vcenters.stopDescription: rvav stops syncing it and building in it, and forgets its inventory.
vcenters.stopConsequences: It is refused while a deployment has VMs there or a placement rule names it. Its VMs stay in vCenter.

nsxManagers.servedNote: The NSX segments and security groups of a vCenter's VMs are made on the NSX Manager serving it. A vCenter none serves can't have them.
nsxManagers.sheetDescription: rvav makes the NSX segments and security groups of its vCenters' VMs on it, with this account.
nsxManagers.nameHint: How rvav calls it, usually its host name
nsxManagers.certHint: A principal identity's, on rvav's servers: instead of the account
nsxManagers.testThenSave: Test again, then save the NSX Manager.
nsxManagers.linkDescription: Deployments made before keep their segments and groups where they are: rvav deletes them there.
nsxManagers.title: NSX Managers
nsxManagers.description: Each vCenter is served by one NSX Manager at most: the segments and security groups of its VMs are made there. A vCenter added later is served by none until you link it.
nsxManagers.emptyBody: Set the NSX connection above, or add an NSX Manager here.
nsxManagers.stopDescription: rvav stops making segments and security groups on it, and its vCenters are served by none.
nsxManagers.stopConsequences: It is refused while deployments have NSX segments or security groups on it. What it has stays in NSX.

identityProvider.issuerHint: As in its tokens, and as the browser reaches it. Entra ID: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0
identityProvider.discoveryHint: Only when rvav reaches the provider at another address than the browser (inside a cluster)
identityProvider.clientIdHint: The web app's client at the provider; tokens must have it as their audience
identityProvider.scopesHint: Space-separated, with openid. Entra ID: also offline_access and a scope of rvav's API, api://<client>/access
identityProvider.groupsClaimHint: The claim group mappings read: groups, or roles for Entra ID's app roles
identityProvider.managerClaimHint: The claim with the user's manager, by email or subject, for approval levels that ask the requester's manager
identityProvider.appliesNow: It applies now: sign-in uses it within a few seconds, without a restart.
identityProvider.localOnly: Only the local administrator and API tokens sign in now.
identityProvider.popupBlocked: The browser blocked the window: allow pop-ups for this site, then try again.
identityProvider.title: Provider settings
identityProvider.about: Everyone but the local administrator signs in here, and gets roles from the groups mapped in <groups>Projects › Identity provider groups</groups>. A saved provider applies without a restart. The local administrator still signs in when it is down.
identityProvider.redirect: Redirect URI, to register at the provider
identityProvider.redirectHint: As a single-page application's (Entra ID: the Single-page application platform; Keycloak: a public client with PKCE). Sign-out comes back to {{origin}}/.
identityProvider.testFirst: Test the provider first: the trial sign-in uses the settings above, before they are saved, in a window of its own.
identityProvider.allPassed: Every check passed: try signing in.
identityProvider.waiting: Sign in at the provider in the new window.
identityProvider.subject: Subject
identityProvider.name: Name
identityProvider.noRoles: None: no group mapping matches, so this user could sign in but do nothing.

day2.description: What people may run on a deployment or a VM besides the built-in actions. Who may run which is set by the <policies>day-2 policies</policies>.
day2.draft: A designed form is a draft
day2.awxWorkflow: AWX workflow <template>{{template}}</template>. Its survey is the form people fill in, unless you design one.
day2.awxJobTemplate: AWX job template <template>{{template}}</template>. Its survey is the form people fill in, unless you design one.
day2.name: Name
day2.nameNeeded: What the action menu says: the action needs one to be saved
day2.everyVm: every VM of the deployment at once
day2.conditionHint: Offered only where this CEL expression is true, for example <cel>{{example}}</cel>. Empty: everywhere.
day2.fromWorkflowsDescription: Workflows registered for day-2 actions on the <workflows>Custom workflows</workflows> page. Their input schema is the form people fill in, unless you design one.
day2.noWorkflowActionsBody: Register a custom workflow for day-2 actions: it becomes an action here.
day2.fromAwxDescription: Templates of rvav's AWX organisation with the day2 label become actions here, every few minutes or when you sync. Their survey is the form people fill in, unless you design one.
day2.noAwxActionsBody: Give a job template or workflow the day2 label in AWX, then sync: it becomes an action here.

day2Form.noneReady: No deployment is ready to preview on.
day2Form.noVmIn: {{name}} has no VM to preview on: choose another deployment.
day2Form.wouldPass: A run with these inputs would pass.
day2Form.wouldHave_one: A run with these inputs would have {{count}} problem.
day2Form.wouldHave_other: A run with these inputs would have {{count}} problems.
day2Form.notReadAgain: The form could not be read again
day2Form.conflict: Someone saved or dropped this form since you opened it. Your last changes are not saved.
day2Form.notDesigned: Not designed yet: this is {{base}}, to start from. Your first change saves a draft.
day2Form.savedActive: Saved: people get this form from their next run.
day2Form.savedDraft: Saved as a draft: people get {{base}} until you turn this form on.
day2Form.failed: Not saved ({{error}}); the next change tries again
day2Form.differSurvey: Where the form and the survey differ
day2Form.differSchema: Where the form and the input schema differ
day2Form.asksForForm: {{name}} asks for this form from its next run
day2Form.fixFirst: Fix the problems the designer marks first.
day2Form.title: {{name}} form
day2Form.description: Once you turn it on, the action's dialog asks for this form instead of {{base}}. Its rules and sources also read what the action runs on, as <mono>resource</mono> and <mono>deployment</mono>.
day2Form.customResource: On a custom resource ({{types}}), <mono>resource</mono> is its <mono>id</mono>, <mono>type</mono>, <mono>name</mono>, <mono>key</mono> and <mono>properties</mono>.
day2Form.wait: Wait for your changes to be saved.
day2Form.dropDescription: {{name}} asks for {{base}} again, from its next run.
day2Form.dropConsequences: The form's fields, rules and sources are deleted.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Where people sign in, the systems rvav connects to and notifies through, and whether EfficientIP agrees with what rvav recorded.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Open one to change its settings and test it. A setting an environment variable sets can't be changed here.

reconcile.title: EfficientIP reconcile
reconcile.description: Compares EfficientIP with what rvav recorded. Nothing is changed.
reconcile.about: It lists the addresses and records tagged for rvav that no deployment owns (for example left by a failed run), and those a deployment owns that EfficientIP no longer has. A request running during the check may show its newest objects here.
reconcile.tagged: EfficientIP has {{addresses}} and {{records}} tagged for rvav.
reconcile.notSet: EfficientIP is not set: it was not compared.
reconcile.ranges: rvav's IP ranges: {{addresses}} of VMs rvav no longer has, {{vms}} on an address their range didn't give.
reconcile.toRanges: Reconcile them on the IP ranges tab
reconcile.cleanBody: Every address and record tagged for rvav belongs to a deployment, and every deployment's addresses and records are in EfficientIP.
reconcile.missingHeading: Owned by a deployment, missing in EfficientIP

page.noSuchBody: rvav doesn't connect to anything called {{kind}}.

about.oidc: Where everyone but the local administrator signs in, and the groups their roles come from.
about.vcenter: Where VMs are built and read, with the console's account and the other vCenters rvav manages.
about.console: The account VM consoles open with, and the WebMKS scripts that show them in the browser.
about.awx: The jobs that configure VMs once built and run day-2 actions, and the inventory token AWX reads rvav with.
about.efficientip: Each VM's IP address and DNS records, and the subnets networks get.
about.nsx: Segments and security groups made for deployments, and their firewall rules.
about.git: The repository rvav keeps the catalog in, one file per item.
about.vra: The vRA that vRA import reads its catalog and deployments from.
about.ad: Where VMs' computer objects are made before they are built, and deleted with them.
about.servicenow: The instance rvav keeps VMs' CIs in, and takes requests from its catalog.
about.smtp: The SMTP server notifications are sent by email through.
about.teams: The bot that sends notifications in Teams, where approvers approve and reject.
about.slack: The app that sends notifications in Slack, where approvers approve and reject.
about.hosts: The hosts REST value sources, a composite's REST calls and webhooks may reach.
about.trust: The CAs every connection trusts besides the system's.

onNextUse.notification: They apply from the next notification.
onNextUse.console: They apply from the next console opened.
onNextUse.vra: They apply from the next read of vRA.
onNextUse.ad: They apply from the next computer object made or deleted.
onNextUse.servicenow: They apply from the next call to ServiceNow.
onNextUse.hosts: They apply from the next call to a host.

setting.gitInsecure: Skip TLS or host key verification

hint.vcenterSync: How often the inventory is read in full; changes come in between, for example 5m or 1h30m (30s to 24h); read on next use
hint.consolePassword: Given again when vCenter's address changes: it only goes to the vCenter it was given for
hint.consoleAccount: A vCenter account that may only open consoles: VMRC links carry a ticket of it
hint.sdkUrls: Comma-separated, in load order; none: VMRC only
hint.awxSync: How often templates are read, for example 5m or 1h30m (30s to 24h); read on next use
hint.efficientipAuth: native, basic or token (an API token: its key ID as the user, its secret as the password)
hint.ipamSync: How often subnets are read, for example 5m or 1h30m (30s to 24h); read on next use
hint.nsxUrl: The NSX Manager, for example https://nsx.corp.example
hint.nsxCertFile: A principal identity instead of a password: its PEM certificate on rvav's hosts
hint.gitCredential: HTTPS: a token. SSH: the deploy key's private key (PEM)
hint.dir: One file per item in it
hint.gitUser: HTTPS: as the server wants it with a token
hint.committer: rvav's commits; the author is the administrator
hint.gitSync: How often the repository is read, for example 5m or 1h30m (30s to 24h); read on next use
hint.vraCredential: With a user, its password; without, a refresh token (an API token)
hint.adUrl: ldaps://dc01.corp.example for LDAPS, or ldap://dc01.corp.example for StartTLS
hint.adUser: Its DN or UPN, for example svc-rvav@corp.example
hint.baseDn: The domain's, for example DC=corp,DC=example: OUs are under it
hint.plainLdap: With ldap://, the service account's password and every object go over the network in the clear. For a lab only.
hint.snowSecret: The user's password, or the OAuth client's secret
hint.snowAuth: basic (a user and its password) or oauth (an OAuth client, by the client credentials grant)
hint.snowUser: With basic: an integration user that may only call web services
hint.cmdb: Made when built, updated after day-2 actions and drift, retired when the VM goes
hint.cmdbClass: A cmdb_ci table, cmdb_ci_vmware_instance by default
hint.dataSource: A value of the discovery_source choice list, rvav by default
hint.projects: Comma-separated IDs or codes of the projects whose VMs are CIs; empty, every project's
hint.snowSync: How often every VM is looked at again and ServiceNow's CIs are read, for example 5m or 1h30m (30s to 24h); read on next use
hint.allowedSources: Comma-separated addresses or networks ServiceNow's calls may come from; empty, any
hint.requestsPerMinute: How many requests ServiceNow may submit a minute, 30 by default
hint.serviceUrl: Where conversations start, for example https://smba.trafficmanager.net/emea
hint.loginUrl: Where the app gets its tokens; another Microsoft cloud's, if not the public one
hint.openidUrl: Its keys check Teams' calls to rvav
hint.apiUrl: Slack's, https://slack.com/api, unless another is used
hint.restHosts: Comma-separated: cmdb.corp.example, *.corp.example, http://host:port for plain http
hint.webhookHosts: Comma-separated, as above: the hosts subscriptions may post to
hint.caBundle: Trusted by every connection besides the system's CAs: a private CA's root or issuing CA. Certificates only, no key

pin.label: Trusted certificate (SHA-256)
pin.hint: A self-signed one, trusted besides the CAs: Trust this certificate, after a test, sets it
pin.inForm: Its SHA-256 is in the form
pin.saveToTrust: Save the settings to trust it, then test again.

integrations.appliesWhenDone: Each process applies them once its running work is done.
integrations.appliesAtStart: They apply when rvav's processes start.
integrations.secretSet: Set; type a new one to replace it
integrations.signingNotSet: Not set: Approve and Reject can't be checked

onboarding.description: VMs in vCenter that rvav doesn't manage. Adopt them into deployments with an owner, a project and a lease, or save a plan that adopts those its filter matches, as they appear.
onboarding.sheetDescription: Nothing changes in vCenter or EfficientIP: rvav records the VMs, and the addresses and DNS records EfficientIP has for them. Deleting a deployment later deletes its VMs and releases those.
onboarding.keepHint: Deleting their deployment is refused until an administrator runs its Allow deletion, as for a blueprint's prevent_delete. For VMs vRA keeps from deletion.
onboarding.adoptedDescription: Each is a deployment like any other: its owner runs its day-2 actions, and its lease runs from when it was made.
onboarding.name: Name
onboarding.atMost: At most {{n}} at once: select fewer to adopt them.
onboarding.noMatch: No VM rvav doesn't manage matches these filters.
onboarding.allManaged: Every VM the inventory has is managed by rvav.

catalogItems.description: Build items, publish their versions and choose which projects may request them.
catalogItems.importedDescription: Templates of rvav's AWX organisation with the catalog label become items, every few minutes or when you sync.
catalogItems.noneYetBody: Give a job template or workflow the catalog label in AWX, then sync: it becomes an item here.

token.title: ServiceNow's token
token.about: ServiceNow calls rvav with an API token that only ServiceNow's endpoints take (<path>/api/v1/servicenow/</path>): it reads the catalog and requests on people's behalf what they may request themselves, nothing more. rvav makes it for a user of its own, valid a year; making a new one revokes the one before.
token.none: None made: ServiceNow can't call rvav.
token.takenFrom_one: Taken from <sources>{{sources}}</sources>, up to {{count}} request a minute: set them in the connection above.
token.takenFrom_other: Taken from <sources>{{sources}}</sources>, up to {{count}} requests a minute: set them in the connection above.
token.takenAny_one: Taken from any address, up to {{count}} request a minute: set them in the connection above.
token.takenAny_other: Taken from any address, up to {{count}} requests a minute: set them in the connection above.
token.putIt: Put it in the API Key credential of ServiceNow's rvav alias. rvav shows it this once.
token.revoked: The token made before is revoked.
token.revokeDescription: ServiceNow can no longer call rvav: its catalog import, order forms and orders fail until you make a new token and put it in ServiceNow.
token.revokeConsequences: Requests already made go on, and rvav still writes their progress to ServiceNow.

cmdb.title: CMDB
cmdb.description: Each VM of the projects chosen is a CI, made when built, updated after day-2 actions and drift, and retired when it goes.
cmdb.reconcilingHint: Refresh the report in a minute.
cmdb.tick: Tick Keep VMs as CIs in the connection above, and save, for rvav to keep VMs in ServiceNow's CMDB.
cmdb.servicenowHas_one: : ServiceNow has {{count}} CI of this source, not retired
cmdb.servicenowHas_other: : ServiceNow has {{count}} CIs of this source, not retired
cmdb.orphansNone: None: every CI of this source that isn't retired is a VM rvav keeps.
cmdb.orphansAll: CIs of this source, not retired, with no VM in rvav. rvav doesn't retire them: decide in ServiceNow.
cmdb.orphansFirst: CIs of this source, not retired, with no VM in rvav (the first {{shown}} of {{total}}). rvav doesn't retire them: decide in ServiceNow.

system.description: rvav as it runs now, read only. Settings saved in <integrations>Integrations</integrations> apply as they say; install settings are changed in the environment.

means.on: approved algorithms where rvav and Go choose

fips.latest: Go's module, not a validated one

processes.title: Processes
processes.description: Each of rvav's processes, and the settings revision it runs.
processes.versions: Processes run {{n}} versions: an upgrade is under way, or a process was left behind.
processes.modes: Processes run in {{n}} FIPS 140-3 modes: give each the same <env>RVAV_FIPS</env>, then start them again.
processes.noneBody: No process has recorded itself in the last 30 seconds. Check that rvav's processes run.

revisions.title: Settings saved in Administration
revisions.description: The latest first, and how far each has applied.
revisions.noneBody: None yet: every setting comes from the environment or its default.

install.title: Install settings
install.description: Set in the environment of each process, as the API answering reads them: change them there, then restart rvav’s processes. A secret’s value is never shown.

password.title: Change the administrator's password
password.what: The install's password is known to whoever installed rvav. Signed in as admin, you choose your own.

provider.title: Set the identity provider
provider.what: Where users sign in: Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta or another OpenID Connect provider. Test it with a trial sign-in before saving.

admin_group.title: Map a group to admin
admin_group.what: Its members administer rvav once they sign in with the provider, so the local account is kept for when the provider is down.

vcenter.title: Connect vCenter
vcenter.what: Where VMs are built, with rvav's service account.

projects.title: Add environments and projects
projects.what: The environments VMs deploy to (development, production, …), the projects that request in them, with their members or groups, and a placement rule for each: where its VMs go.

ipam.title: Connect EfficientIP
ipam.what: Each VM's address and DNS records.

awx.title: Connect AWX
awx.what: The jobs that configure VMs once built, and day-2 actions.

catalog_item.title: Publish a first catalog item
catalog_item.what: What users request: a VM blueprint, an AWX job or both. Then the templates, networks and placement it needs, in Templates and networks.

setup.hidden: The checklist won't open at sign-in
setup.hiddenBody: It stays here, in Administration › Setup.
setup.shown: The checklist opens at sign-in again
setup.localOnly: Sign in with the local admin account to change it.
setup.description: The steps that get a first request through. Each opens its page, and is ticked once that page has what it needs.
setup.complete: Every step is done: users can sign in and request. The checklist no longer opens at sign-in.

branding.description: The portal's name, accent colour and logos. Everyone sees them, on the sign-in page too, and emails carry them.
branding.own: rvav's own accent, in both themes.
branding.readsSame: Reads at {{ratio}}:1 in the light theme. The dark theme takes it as it is so that its text reads too.
branding.readsLighter: Reads at {{ratio}}:1 in the light theme. The dark theme takes {{dark}}, lighter so that its text reads too.
branding.nameAccentDescription: The menu, the sign-in page, the browser's title and emails show the name. Buttons, links and focus rings take the accent.
branding.portalNameHint: Up to 40 characters. Left empty, the portal is called rvav.
branding.accentHint: The light theme's, as #rrggbb: text in it needs a contrast of 4.5:1. Left empty, rvav's own.
branding.fallbackLight: The light theme's logo is shown.
branding.shown: Shown in the menu and on the sign-in page.
branding.tooLarge: {{name}} is larger than 256 KB, the most a logo is.
branding.logosDescription: PNG, JPEG or SVG, 256 KB and 2048 pixels a side at most. An SVG with scripts, links or external pictures is refused. Emails show the light theme's logo when it is a PNG or a JPEG.

audit.description: Every change people and rvav make: catalog, projects, policies, settings and tokens. Newest first.
audit.nothingYetBody: Changes to the catalog, projects, policies, settings and tokens show here as people make them.

auditForwarding.sheetDescription: rvav sends it each audit event written from now on, in order, and keeps those it couldn't send until it can.
auditForwarding.name: Name
auditForwarding.appNameHint: The APP-NAME of each message, rvav when empty
auditForwarding.caHint: PEM. The CAs that sign the server's certificate, besides the system's and rvav's CA bundle
auditForwarding.certHint: PEM. What rvav presents when the server asks for a certificate, with its key below
auditForwarding.keyHint: The stored secret that holds the key in PEM (Catalog items › Secrets)
auditForwarding.urlHint: On a host webhooks may call (Integrations › Allowed hosts)
auditForwarding.secretHint: Each call is signed with it in X-Rvav-Signature, as subscriptions' webhooks are
auditForwarding.testNote: The test event, settings.audit_destination.test with the ID test, went once: the events waiting aren't affected. The audit log records the test.
auditForwarding.description: Syslog servers and webhooks, such as your SIEM's, that get a copy of each audit event. Events wait in rvav until they are delivered; the audit log keeps them all the same.
auditForwarding.emptyBody: Send audit events to a syslog server over TLS, or to a webhook, to keep them in your SIEM.
auditForwarding.dropped_one: The event waiting for it is dropped. The audit log keeps it.
auditForwarding.dropped_other: The {{n}} events waiting for it are dropped. The audit log keeps them.
auditForwarding.keepsAll: The audit log keeps every event.
